APIKeyLeaderboardResponse.description: Only billable catalog usage. Key identifiers are opaque, never secrets.
APIKeyLeaderboardResponse.title: APIKeyLeaderboardResponse

APIKeyModelUsage.description:
One model's share of an API key's usage in the window, with its cost.

`rate_key` is the catalog model the traffic was billed under. The cost is
rated per day at that model's own price; `amount=None` with
`priced=False` means no price was in force ("not yet priced", never 0), and
`partial` means only part of the usage was priced (the amount is a floor).
APIKeyModelUsage.title: APIKeyModelUsage

BillingLine.description:
One model's share of a bill.

`priced` is per-line and not derived from the amount: an unpriced model must
render "not yet priced", never a zero that reads as free.
BillingLine.title: BillingLine

CatalogBillingResponse.description:
Showback for one tenant, one line per model.

A single total is no longer enough: one key now spans every listed model, so
a tenant that cannot see which model spent the money cannot act on the
number. `partial` means at least one line is unpriced, so the total is a
floor and not the bill.

disclaimer.default: Preview — usage-based estimate, not an invoice.
disclaimer.title: Disclaimer

CatalogBillingResponse.title: CatalogBillingResponse

CatalogCapabilitiesResponse.description:
Advisory: what the caller may do in the catalog.

Lets the console state the admin gate up front rather than letting a tenant
fill in a listing form and only then be refused. Purely presentational —
the commands re-check, so this grants nothing.
CatalogCapabilitiesResponse.title: CatalogCapabilitiesResponse

CatalogListingCard.description:
The descriptive card an admin attaches when listing a model.

Context window and region were dropped from this surface: both were free
text an admin retyped per listing, so they were authored once and then went
stale against the thing they described -- the context window in particular
is a property of the running engine, which already reports it and refuses
an over-long prompt with the real number. The columns remain in the table,
unwritten, so restoring them is a schema-free change if they come back as
derived values rather than typed ones.
CatalogListingCard.title: CatalogListingCard

CatalogModelCapabilities.description: Optional facts an admin publishes about a catalog model.
CatalogModelCapabilities.title: CatalogModelCapabilities

ConsumerUsageRow.description: Admin view: one tenant's consumption of one listed model.
ConsumerUsageRow.title: ConsumerUsageRow

CorrectCatalogModelPricingRequest.description:
Operator: re-price a model's retained usage from `retroactive_from`.

The one audited exception to "a price never re-rates history". Appends a
correction row to the price book (nothing is updated or deleted); it is
also the price in force from now on. `reason` is required and stored with
the row as the audit trail. Ordinary `SetCatalogModelPricing` still refuses
any backdated or re-rating version.
CorrectCatalogModelPricingRequest.title: CorrectCatalogModelPricingRequest

CreateInferenceRuntimeConfigRequest.description:
Runtime overrides for create, including the env composition contract.

Omitted preserves legacy overlay behavior. A caller that rendered a complete
environment can request replacement so recipe-only variables do not become
part of the stored configuration unseen.

sgl_router_additional_args.description: Router argv overrides. Omit to preserve; [] restores platform defaults.
sgl_router_additional_args.title: Sgl Router Additional Args

sgl_router_env.description: Complete custom router environment. Omit to preserve; {} clears it.
sgl_router_env.title: Sgl Router Env

CreateInferenceRuntimeConfigRequest.title: CreateInferenceRuntimeConfigRequest

EnvStrategy.description:
How a CREATE composes the caller's ``env`` with the recipe's.

Wire values; never change one.
EnvStrategy.title: EnvStrategy

force_api.description: Skip direct retrieval and use the provider APIs when direct content is incomplete.
force_api.title: Force Api

InferenceConfigurationOptionResponse.description:
A deployment recipe as an option a tenant can actually choose.

`name`, `model_family` and `serving_pattern` are here because the create form
cannot work without them, and this DTO is the only answer it gets: the picker
labels each row `name · serving_pattern`, submits the `name` as the recipe,
and filters the list to recipes whose `model_family` matches the chosen model
(a Qwen model listing `deepseek-pd` is an option create would then reject).
Projected away, every row renders blank and none of them can be selected —
the whole deploy flow stops at an empty dropdown.

main's reduction dropped them because main had no recipe picker to serve.
They disclose nothing this response does not already: `default_configuration`
is published in full right below, and it carries `command`, `model_path` and
`env`. A recipe's own name is strictly less than that.
InferenceConfigurationOptionResponse.title: InferenceConfigurationOptionResponse

InferenceConfigurationPreviewResponse.description:
Read-only preview of the configuration a create would deploy.

Exactly one field: the resolved configuration, already passed through the
same positive public allowlist as the instance DTOs. The internal result also
carries the operator-complete configuration used for rollback; none of it is
projected here.
InferenceConfigurationPreviewResponse.title: InferenceConfigurationPreviewResponse

InferenceInvocationResponse.description:
One relayed call to the public OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

`response` is the upstream body verbatim -- it is the caller's own inference
result, not platform state. `upstream_status` is preserved separately because
the control-plane envelope always answers 200; without it a caller cannot
tell a rejected API key (401/403) from a model error.
InferenceInvocationResponse.title: InferenceInvocationResponse

InferenceKeyPublicResponse.description:
Metadata for one tenant API key. Never the token.

`tenant_id` is dropped: the route is tenant-scoped, so it can only ever echo
the caller's own tenant back at it.

The expiry is published as `valid_until` rather than `expires_at`.
`expires_at` is on the reviewed contract's prohibited list because it names a
reader lease's internal liveness deadline; a credential's own expiry is
genuinely user-facing -- a user cannot rotate a key whose end date it cannot
see -- so it is published under a name that is not the banned one.

`scoped_instances` is Optional and NOT defaulted to []: None means an
unscoped, tenant-wide key that calls every model, while [] is an empty
allowlist that authorizes nothing. Collapsing the two would invert the
meaning of the most permissive key in the system.
InferenceKeyPublicResponse.title: InferenceKeyPublicResponse

InferenceKeyRevocationResponse.description:
Acknowledgement that a key was revoked.

The revoke route used to answer with a bare `dict`, which publishes no schema
at all. This mirrors the `*ActionResponse` shape the other domains use, keyed
by the same `lookup_id` the caller passed in.
InferenceKeyRevocationResponse.title: InferenceKeyRevocationResponse

InferenceKeyScopeResponse.description:
One deployment a key is restricted to, resolved for display.

A key is scoped to the named instance's POOL, so every live member of that
pool is listed. `stale` is not cosmetic: once the pool has no live member
the key silently authorizes nothing, and a bare id list would render that
expired grant as though it still worked.
InferenceKeyScopeResponse.title: InferenceKeyScopeResponse

InferenceLiveEditResponse.description:
Whether the API would refuse a live edit of this endpoint right now.

Single-pool endpoints only (PD publishes ``pd_live_edit``). Computed by the
rule the update path enforces under the instance row lock
(`domain/inference_live_roll.py`), from the same row: ``edit`` is the
reason ANY live edit is refused -- a change is still rolling out
(``INFERENCE_LIVE_RECONFIGURATION_ROLL_IN_PROGRESS``). ``null`` means
allowed.
InferenceLiveEditResponse.title: InferenceLiveEditResponse

InferenceLogsPublicResponse.description:
Container logs for one deployment, read through the backend.

Field-for-field the same as the internal DTO, because every field on it is
already user data: there is no attempt timeline, no namespace, no pod name
and no dashboard url to strip. `degraded` is load-bearing -- without it an
empty `logs` cannot be told apart from "the log store was unreachable", and a
UI would report "no logs" for an outage.
InferenceLogsPublicResponse.title: InferenceLogsPublicResponse

InferenceMetricsPublicResponse.description:
Live serving metrics for one deployment.

`pools` arrives already reduced by `project_public_inference_pools` (role,
ready, desired, live, status) -- images, argv, env, mounts, probes and
networking never reach this DTO. The `grafana_*_url` fields are expiring,
tenant-scoped embed tickets minted server-side after ownership is proven.
Null means "not configured", which a UI renders as no link rather than a
dead one.

`pd_metrics` (PD only) is keyed by role. Its `router` entry is scraped from
the endpoint's own sgl-router, which only probes pool readiness: PD traffic
is served through the tenant's shared model gateway, so the router's
counters are NOT request throughput. `pd_metrics_router_scope` says so
explicitly ("readiness") whenever a `router` entry is present.
InferenceMetricsPublicResponse.title: InferenceMetricsPublicResponse

InferenceOperationPublicResponse.description:
Progress of one accepted lifecycle operation.

`fence_token` and `lease_expires_at` are dropped: both belong to the worker
lease that fences concurrent reconcilers, and neither is actionable by the
caller. `revision_id` stays because it is the join back to
GetInferenceRevision -- it is what makes "which change is this?" answerable.
`source_operation_id` provides the same safe join for automatic rollbacks
without exposing the internal idempotency key.
InferenceOperationPublicResponse.title: InferenceOperationPublicResponse

InferencePdLiveEditResponse.description:
Whether the API would refuse a live edit of this PD endpoint right now.

Computed by the same rule the update path enforces under the instance row
lock (`domain/inference_pd_live_roll.py`), from the same row: ``edit`` is
the reason ANY live edit is refused (a roll is in flight), ``runtime`` the
reason a change to what the pods run is refused (a pool below 2, or not
Ready at its size). ``null`` means allowed. A mixed resize depends on the
edit itself and is not reported here.
InferencePdLiveEditResponse.title: InferencePdLiveEditResponse

InferencePoolStatusResponse.description:
One serving pool's status (PD: prefill or decode).

``desired`` is what the workload has APPLIED now and ``target`` what the
endpoint is configured for; they differ on purpose while a roll-then-shrink
holds a shrinking pool at its live size. ``ready``/``desired`` are absent
when that pool has not been observed.
InferencePoolStatusResponse.title: InferencePoolStatusResponse

InferenceRevisionPublicResponse.description:
One immutable desired-state revision.

`spec_digest`, `artifact_manifest_digest` and `controller_kind` are dropped.
The two digests are reconciliation bookkeeping -- the tracker compares them
to decide whether to re-apply -- and `controller_kind` names the Kubernetes
object (Deployment vs LeaderWorkerSet) that renders the revision, which is
the same class of fact as `deployment_name`. `effective_spec` is already
reduced to the tenant-visible launch knobs by the internal DTO's validator.
InferenceRevisionPublicResponse.title: InferenceRevisionPublicResponse

InferenceRuntimeConfigPublicResponse.description:
The image, env and engine flags a deployment actually runs.

Readable by anyone with view permission on the instance (owner decision
2026-10-21), scoped to the caller's own tenant -- not admin-only. Everything
here is already settable by the same caller through create and the
runtime-config PATCH, so gating the read while the write is open would only
make the surface harder to reason about. Live container ENV is never
returned.
InferenceRuntimeConfigPublicResponse.title: InferenceRuntimeConfigPublicResponse

InferenceRuntimePoolOverridePublicRespon.description:
One PD pool's complete runtime. Mirrors the internal model
field-for-field (the public contract is fail-closed).
InferenceRuntimePoolOverridePublicRespon.title: InferenceRuntimePoolOverridePublicResponse

InferenceRuntimePoolOverrideRequest.description:
One PD pool's runtime. Omitted field = unchanged (at create: the recipe
value); ``null`` or an empty value clears it. ``env`` and ``additional_args``
are the COMPLETE pool values (at create, ``env`` merges over the recipe env
unless ``env_strategy`` is ``replace``).
InferenceRuntimePoolOverrideRequest.title: InferenceRuntimePoolOverrideRequest

InferenceRuntimePoolPublicResponse.description:
One serving pool's live container identity, as published.

Mirrors the internal model field-for-field on purpose: the public contract is
fail-closed, so an unlisted field is dropped rather than forwarded. Adding a
field to the internal DTO alone silently publishes nothing.

Live container ENV is absent here for the same reason it is absent
internally -- it can carry provider tokens and signed URLs, including ones no
current release knows to redact.
InferenceRuntimePoolPublicResponse.title: InferenceRuntimePoolPublicResponse

InferenceStatusDetailResponse.description:
The derived status view (``status_view.derive_status_view``), typed.

Was a free-form ``dict`` (``additionalProperties: true``), which the public
field allowlist could not inspect. Every key it ever carried is kept, with
its spelling; a key not declared here is dropped (``extra="ignore"``).
``availability`` says whether the attached endpoint can serve NEW requests
now (Available / Unavailable / Unknown), separately from the lifecycle
``status`` and the rollout ``phase``.
InferenceStatusDetailResponse.title: InferenceStatusDetailResponse

ListingPricing.description:
What a listing costs, straight from the price book in force.

Deliberately the same row that `rate_rollups` bills against (keyed by
`rate_key`), so the number a tenant is quoted before calling a model and the
number they are charged afterwards cannot drift apart.

`cached_input_price_per_million` is the cache-read rate. None means no
cached rate is in force, which bills cache hits at the full input rate --
not free. A listing with no price row at all yields `pricing=None`, which
the UI must render as "not yet priced" rather than as zero.

An all-zero block is a different answer from None and renders differently:
it is a price row an admin wrote, so the model really is free.
ListingPricing.title: ListingPricing

MintedInferenceKeyPublicResponse.description:
The one and only time the plaintext token exists.

`token` is public BY DESIGN and only here: the server stores a hash, so a key
that is not read from this response can never be recovered. `lookup_id` is
the durable handle used to list and revoke it.
MintedInferenceKeyPublicResponse.title: MintedInferenceKeyPublicResponse

OpenAIModelCard.description:
One row of `GET /v1/models`: the OpenAI model object, plus the catalog.

The first four fields are OpenAI's and are named OpenAI's way, because the
point of this shape is that an unmodified SDK can read it. `id` is the string
a caller puts in a request body's `model` field -- the listing's model_id,
NOT its rate_key (the rate_key is the billing identity; sending it as `model`
fails to dispatch).

The rest is the catalog card. The published docs promise that this endpoint
returns "the available models, each context length, and current status", and
a bare OpenAI object carries none of that. Extra fields are safe for SDK
compatibility: OpenAI clients ignore members they do not know, and the four
they require are unchanged.

Deliberately NO pricing. A Platform API key grants discovery, not access to
commercial rates. Price stays on the console's CAS-authenticated catalog read.
OpenAIModelCard.title: OpenAIModelCard

OpenAIModelList.description:
The envelope OpenAI clients expect: `{"object": "list", "data": [...]}`.

Deliberately NOT wrapped in the platform's `Response[...]`. That envelope is
what the console reads, and an OpenAI SDK pointed at a wrapped body sees no
`data[].id` and reports zero models.
OpenAIModelList.title: OpenAIModelList

PriceCorrectionResponse.description: The appended correction row: the price, where it applies from, and why.
PriceCorrectionResponse.title: PriceCorrectionResponse

ProblemResponse.description: RFC 7807 problem details returned by public APIs.
ProblemResponse.title: ProblemResponse

RequestEventResponse.description:
One ledger row. METADATA ONLY — no prompt or completion text exists in
this table, so none can be returned here even by mistake.
RequestEventResponse.title: RequestEventResponse

inference_instance_ids.description: For inference keys only: restrict access to these self-hosted instances. Omit for all models within the key's audience.
inference_instance_ids.title: Inference Instance Ids

username.description: Free-text label for whoever this key is for, e.g. a person's username. Display only -- it grants nothing.
username.title: Username

RpcGetAPIKeyUsageLeaderboardRequest.description: Half-open UTC day range, at most 90 days. Defaults to 30 days including today.
RpcGetAPIKeyUsageLeaderboardRequest.title: RpcGetAPIKeyUsageLeaderboardRequest

RpcGetTenantCatalogBillingRequest.description: Operator-only, half-open UTC day range; 30 days by default, at most 90.
RpcGetTenantCatalogBillingRequest.title: RpcGetTenantCatalogBillingRequest

RpcListUserInferenceKeysRequest.description:
Support/operator: one user of one tenant, both explicit (never the caller's).

`user_id` is the CAS User id; a key belongs to it only when the key's
immutable owner principal names that User in `tenant_id`.
RpcListUserInferenceKeysRequest.title: RpcListUserInferenceKeysRequest

RpcResolveSupportRequestLineageRequest.description: One exact tenant-scoped selector; native session IDs are correlation only.
RpcResolveSupportRequestLineageRequest.title: RpcResolveSupportRequestLineageRequest

RpcUpdateInferenceRuntimeConfigRequest.description:
Tenant-scoped runtime edit (UpdateInferenceInstance), RPC shape.

Subclasses the REST body so the two cannot drift, and adds the id the RPC
envelope needs. The handler rebuilds a clean REST body with
`exclude_unset=True`: an omitted field must stay OMITTED, because the PATCH
treats omitted as unchanged and a blanked `env` would take a running
deployment down.

sgl_router_additional_args.description: Router argv overrides. Omit to preserve; [] restores platform defaults.
sgl_router_additional_args.title: Sgl Router Additional Args

sgl_router_env.description: Complete custom router environment. Omit to preserve; {} clears it.
sgl_router_env.title: Sgl Router Env

RpcUpdateInferenceRuntimeConfigRequest.title: RpcUpdateInferenceRuntimeConfigRequest

max_results.description: Requested count, clamped to 1–5. Omit for five results.
max_results.title: Max Results

SetListingPricingRequest.description:
Admin: set the price for a listing, versioned by `effective_from`.

Writes a new price-book row rather than updating one. Rating joins usage to
the price in force at each bucket's own time, so a price change must never
rewrite what a tenant was already charged.

Everything defaults, and that is deliberate: this is also the block that
rides along with a listing, where an admin who types no numbers is saying
"this model is free" rather than leaving the price unknown. The default is
only safe because it is written as a REAL row -- a listing with no row at
all still means "not yet priced" and must never render as 0.
SetListingPricingRequest.title: SetListingPricingRequest

SupportAttemptResponse.description: One guard-observed attempt, NOT a response/recovery/billing receipt.
SupportAttemptResponse.title: SupportAttemptResponse

SupportRequestLineageResponse.description:
Bounded matching attempts, never an assertion that a case is local-only.

Selector values, tenant identity, API-key attribution, grants and bodies are
not echoed. Same Support ID does not prove all matches are the same logical
request. Empty means only that this seven-day projection has no match.
SupportRequestLineageResponse.title: SupportRequestLineageResponse

UpdateInferenceRuntimeConfigRequest.description:
Runtime edit: any user of the instance's tenant whom CAS grants
UpdateInferenceInstance on it (not only its creator, not catalog-admin). Every field optional; omitted means unchanged.

Carries every member of OPERATOR_INFERENCE_CONFIGURATION_KEYS.
`command`/`args` are absent on purpose: argv belongs to the catalog recipe,
and a per-instance override would drift silently from the recipe every
future deploy is rendered from.

sgl_router_additional_args.description: Router argv overrides. Omit to preserve; [] restores platform defaults.
sgl_router_additional_args.title: Sgl Router Additional Args

sgl_router_env.description: Complete custom router environment. Omit to preserve; {} clears it.
sgl_router_env.title: Sgl Router Env

UpdateInferenceRuntimeConfigRequest.title: UpdateInferenceRuntimeConfigRequest

UsageSummary.description: Totals over the window, plus the honesty flags the UI must surface.
UsageSummary.title: UsageSummary

UserInferenceKeysResponse.description:
Support/operator view of every key one user owns in one tenant.

`keys` lists every owned key in any status (active, expired, revoked), by
`lookup_id`, with the same fields as the tenant key list -- never a token or
hash. `active_count` is exactly how many of them RevokeUserInferenceKeys would
revoke now: keys whose `status` is `active`, INCLUDING ones whose
`valid_until` has passed (expiry does not change the stored status).
UserInferenceKeysResponse.title: UserInferenceKeysResponse

UserInferenceKeysRevocationResponse.description:
Every active key the user owned is now revoked.

Returned only when nothing is known to remain active; otherwise the call
fails with a 503 problem that names what was and was not revoked. A repeat
call answers `revoked_count: 0`.
UserInferenceKeysRevocationResponse.title: UserInferenceKeysRevocationResponse

ValidateInferenceKeyPublicResponse.description:
Whether an API key is live, and whose it is labelled as.

Published verbatim rather than reduced: `tenant_id` is normally dropped from
a public DTO because a tenant-scoped route can only echo the caller's own
tenant back, but this route is UNAUTHENTICATED and has no caller tenant --
identifying the key's tenant is the entire purpose.

`tenant_id` and `username` are populated only when `valid` is true; every
failure answers with the bare `{"valid": false}` so the endpoint cannot be
used to tell a real key from an unknown one.
ValidateInferenceKeyPublicResponse.title: ValidateInferenceKeyPublicResponse

post.description:
Any viewer of the instance (ReadInferenceInstance), tenant-scoped by the
REST handler this delegates to. Not admin-only.
Operator only: every key one user owns in one tenant, in this region.

Operator only: revoke every active key one user owns in one tenant.

200 means nothing the user owns is still active in this region. Any doubt
is a 503 problem whose `revoked_lookup_ids` / `unrevoked_lookup_ids` say
exactly what happened; repeating the call is safe and retries the rest.

Tenant-scoped (UpdateInferenceInstance), as the REST handler. Rebuilds the REST body preserving which fields were SET, so an
omitted field stays unchanged rather than being cleared.
UNAUTHENTICATED because the inference key is the credential.

Operator: audited price correction that re-prices retained usage.

Master key or root tenant only (same boundary as tier management). The
correction is appended to the price book and committed; it never edits or
deletes an earlier version. Every call is audit-logged with its reason.

post.summary: Get Tenant Api Key Usage Leaderboard

post.description:
Read matching guard-observed attempts, including authenticated denials.

This is a restricted support lookup, not a tenant API. It returns only the
metadata required to continue tracing and never echoes the Support ID,
tenant ID, API-key attribution, grant, prompt, response, or body.

Operator-only (privileged gate): re-run provisioning, incl. from FAILED.

A re-send while the repair runs answers 202 with no second operation; 409
when no operation is in flight and a quota operation holds the tenant or
the workspace is DELETING.

get.description:
Platform-key-authenticated OpenAI-compatible model discovery.

This is what `GET /v1/models` on the catalog host is rewritten to, and what
the published docs promise. Three things about it are deliberate.

NOT the OpenAI path directly, and NOT proxied to the router. A GET rule on
the catalog HTTPRoute would send a bodiless request to sgl-model-gateway,
where modelguard short-circuits (no body to dispatch on), the shared host has
no model id and a catalog key has no scopes -- so the scope test is skipped
and the admin router answers with its ENTIRE model list, de-listed models
included. See CATALOG_ROUTE_PATHS. Serving discovery from the platform is the
only way to answer this question without that exposure, because only the
platform knows what is LISTED as opposed to what is loaded.

NOT wrapped in `Response[...]`. An OpenAI SDK reads `data[].id` off the top
level; the platform envelope would make every client report zero models.

The Platform API key is the credential, not a CAS console session. Discovery
carries no pricing or internal identifiers; those stay on the console catalog.

post.description:
How much of each window budget a tenant has used (D-SB-11).

Without ``tenant_id`` the caller's own tenant (Console); with it, Support
(root tenant or master key) may name any tenant and the read is audited,
everyone else only their own. The figures are the enforcer's estimates; a
PDP failure is 503 and the caller shows the usage as unavailable.
